narrative.benchmark_md: Five peers were selected and locked during the Research Phase (Batch 1) and are immutable throughout the assessment. Peers are scored at category level using public evidence. Peer medians are calculated as the arithmetic median of the five peer category scores. IMA's gap to the peer median is reported for each category and pillar. The peer set was selected on the basis of: Insurance Broker subvertical match, size tier proximity (LARGE T2), geographic overlap (US multi-state), and competitive relevance (PitchBook, Tracxn, and CIAB membership).
narrative.issue_register_md: Eight issues identified during the Research Phase and confirmed in the Assessment Phase (Phase 3). ISS-001 is the only MATERIAL issue — discovered via a B5D proxy validation search (not captured in initial public evidence batches). This is the most consequential risk factor. All caps have been applied to final capability scores in Column D and Column I of the DMA Workbook.

per_pillar_md.P1: Five categories evaluated across 184 capability. P1 scores above peer median in 4 of 5 categories, with Innovation leading the entire peer set by a full maturity level.
per_pillar_md.P2: Four categories evaluated across 228 capability — the largest capability count of any pillar. P2 carries the highest Weighting (35%) because client experience quality IS the commercial differentiator in a fee-for-advice broker model.
per_pillar_md.P3: Four categories across 116 capability. P3 leads peers in three of four categories. Business Resilience is the only below-peer category and creates the most commercially consequential internal gap given the CVRM advisory practice.
per_pillar_md.P4: Four categories across 174 capability. P4 has the narrowest peer advantage (+0.05) but contains both IMA's strongest architecture foundation (, 2.97) and the most strategically consequential gap in the assessment ( Analytics & AI, 2.02).
